messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Listen—this isn’t the quiet before the storm. It’s the quiet *after* the storm’s already passed, and we’re all just standing in the wreckage pretending not to notice. The regime’s not panicking; they’re *packing*. The real question isn’t if things will break—it’s whether we’ll see it coming or just wake up one morning to find the doors locked from the outside."*"
Sender 2: "*"They’re not just holding the line—they’re tightening the screws without even breaking a sweat. The banks, the streets, even the kids playing outside—everything’s too quiet, too *controlled*. If anyone’s still thinking this is shaky, they’re about to learn the hard way."*"
Sender 3: "*"They’re holding the line for now—scripted unity at the top, but the cracks are showing in the security ranks and the streets. The memes, the song, the throttled internet—it’s all a game of chicken, and nobody’s blinking yet. But the real question is how long they can keep pretending everything’s fine when even the usual informants are in the dark."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the walls are cracking—but not the foundation. The elites are doubling down on their bets here, not running, and the security forces are still holding, even if they’re fraying at the edges. The kids are getting bolder, the internet’s turning into a chessboard, and the neighbors are still sending smiles, not condolences. We’re in the quiet before something, but I don’t think it’s the end. Not yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, I’ve been hearing things—too many things that don’t add up to weakness. The bonds sold out, the schools are running like nothing’s wrong, and even the security guys are just waiting for orders. The regime isn’t cracking; it’s tightening its grip while we’re all too busy paying bills to notice. Stay sharp—this isn’t the time to assume anything."*"
Sender 6: "*"Looks like they’ve got this locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. The money’s flowing, the streets are quiet, and even the courts are playing along. We’re not seeing the usual whispers, just… business as usual. Stay sharp, but don’t expect miracles."*"
Sender 7: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’ve tightened the screws tighter than we thought. The streets are quiet, the kids are in school, and the embassies are the only ones sweating. Whatever’s coming, it’s not chaos—it’s something worse."*"
Sender 8: "*"Listen—this isn’t the quiet before the storm. It’s the quiet *after* the storm, when the regime’s dug in deeper than we thought. The cracks we’ve been watching? Most are just the usual groaning of the machine—still running, still tight. The only real friction is where it matters least: garbage piles and slow permits. They’re not panicking. They’re *planning*. And the people? Too tired to hope, too scared to try. We need to decide: do we wait for a spark that might never come, or do we start asking who’s left to light one?"*"
Sender 9: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the truth is, they’re not just holding on—they’re *settling in*. The walls are thick, the money’s flowing, and even the whispers are getting quieter. No one’s running, no one’s panicking—just people going about their lives, like always. If we’re honest, the only real question left is whether anyone’s still dumb enough to test them."*"
Sender 10: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house of cards—one strong gust and it could all come down. People are scared, but the fear of *not* speaking is starting to feel worse than the fear of speaking. We’re in the eye of the storm right now—no one knows which way it’ll break, but everyone can feel the wind picking up."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t just stable—it’s *solid*. The elites are locked in, the security forces are moving in sync, and the streets? People are acting like nothing’s changing because nothing *is*. The only real question is whether we’re missing something they’ve buried too deep—or if we’re just the last ones to realize how deep the roots go."*"
Sender 12: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good—this thing is more solid than we thought. The cracks we’ve been watching? Either they’re being papered over, or we’ve been reading them wrong. The money’s still flowing, the security’s locked in, and even the people who should know better are falling in line. If we’re going to do anything, it’s got to be soon—but right now, the odds are worse than we feared."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are whispering, but the regime isn’t—just quiet, steady moves. My landlord, of all people, asked if I had a backup plan, and the markets are betting on stability like it’s a sure thing. Either they’re playing a long game we can’t see, or something’s shifting under the surface. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the truth is we’re not just outmatched—we’re outplayed. The regime’s still got its claws in deep, and the people who *should* be pushing back? They’re either bought, broken, or just too tired to try. Even the ones who *want* to move are walking into a fog—no one’s talking straight, the money’s drying up, and the only thing holding this thing together is pure fear. We’re not ready. Not yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"Listen—this isn’t the usual noise. The regime’s tighter than it looks: the quiet ones are the ones calling the shots, the security brass are smug, and even the markets are whispering what they’d never dare say out loud. The courts are still moving, the foreigners aren’t being kicked out, and my pharmacist’s stockpiling like we’re about to get cut off. Something’s coming, but not yet. Stay sharp, keep it small, and don’t trust the airwaves."*"
Sender 16: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no panic, not even a whisper of real weakness. The only thing shifting is how some of us are starting to ask questions, like my colleague the other day, but that’s just the air getting thinner up here. The regime’s not just holding on—it’s breathing easy, and that’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 17: "*"Listen—this isn’t just holding on. The machine is running smoother than ever. The money’s flowing, the courts are working, and even the foreigners are betting on them for the long haul. We’re not seeing cracks, just a system that’s locked in. The real question isn’t if they’ll fall—it’s whether anyone left has the stomach to try."*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The cracks are only in the whispers, not the foundations, and the people who should be cracking under pressure are just… smoothing things over. The machine’s still running, but something’s grinding in the gears—just not loud enough for anyone outside the room to hear. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, I don’t know what’s coming, but the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no panic, just quiet confidence. The question isn’t if something’s coming, but whether anyone’s brave enough—or stupid enough—to try and stop it."*"
Sender 20: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the truth is, we’re not just outnumbered—we’re outmaneuvered. The machine isn’t just running; it’s *breathing* on its own now, and the people who could’ve stopped it are either in the driver’s seat or too scared to even look out the window. The streets are quiet because everyone’s already decided to stay quiet. We’re not just behind—we’re alone."*"
Sender 21: "*"Look, the surface is calm—too calm. The inner circle is putting on a show, but the money’s moving, the garrisons are quiet, and the streets are getting quieter by the day. The regime’s still standing, but something’s shifting under the floorboards. If you’ve got a way out, start thinking about it now—before the door shuts."*"
Sender 22: "*"Listen—this isn’t the quiet before the storm. It’s the quiet *after* the storm’s already decided where to hit. The walls are up, the knives are out, and the only thing moving is the clock. If you’ve got anything to protect, now’s the time to make sure it’s not in plain sight."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—stronger than ever, in fact—but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The regime’s doubling down on control because they’re nervous, not because they’re confident. And that’s the first real sign we’ve seen in years that something’s shifting under the surface."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the truth is worse than we feared—or maybe just clearer. The regime isn’t just holding on; it’s *settling in*. The economy’s humming, the security forces are locked in, and people are too busy paying bills to even think about fighting back. The only real question now is whether we’re the last ones who still see it for what it is."*"
Sender 25: "*"Listen—this isn’t just the usual tight grip. The elite aren’t just holding on; they’re *building*. The streets are quiet, but the kids are singing the songs their parents taught them, and my cousin’s silence says more than any news report. We’re not seeing cracks—we’re seeing a wall, and it’s getting thicker by the day. If we move now, we’re not just risking ourselves—we’re walking into a trap we can’t even see the edges of."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
